page: Amazon Web Services m6id.large is a general-purpose virtual instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It is configured with an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at a base clock of 3.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance provides 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyperthreading enabled, alongside 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Dedicated hardware extensions include AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and cryptographic flags such as AES and SHA_NI. An integrated 118 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume is bundled directly with the host, while network bandwidth provides a baseline speed of 1 Gbps. There is no discrete GPU acceleration included.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent single-thread execution alongside constraints typical of dual-vCPU entry profiles. Single-core performance achieves middle-tier results, reaching 1880.08 in stress-ng and 1489.0 in Geekbench single-core, supported by a 28.04 GB/sec rate in single-threaded gzip compression. However, overall multi-core aggregate throughput falls into the lower tiers, reflecting the 2-vCPU hardware footprint. Geekbench multi-core registers at 1757.0 and PassMark CPU score reaches 2956.85. Memory bandwidth reaches 103.27 GB/sec for small cached blocks, declining to 14.72 GB/sec read and 12.37 GB/sec write on larger uncached working sets.

Application and system benchmarks mirror this entry-level capacity. Redis SET operations achieve 1.97 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures at 3.58 GB/sec. Small 135M parameter LLM inference delivers 139.48 tokens per second during prompt processing and 50.55 tokens per second for generation. PassMark database operations and clang compilation scores remain in the lower percentiles due to limited thread density.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, the m6id.large trades aggregate compute capacity for low-latency, integrated NVMe local storage. This configuration fits lightweight caching layers, development environments, transient build storage, microservices, and web application nodes requiring high-speed temporary disk access without the overhead of external EBS volumes. It is not suitable for parallel computational jobs, large-scale databases, or high-concurrency production workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services m6id.large is an x86_64 general-purpose instance featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single physical Intel Xeon 8375C core at 3.5 GHz and 8.0 GB of DDR4 RAM. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it includes 118 GB of bundled NVMe SSD instance storage and a 1 Gbps baseline network interface without discrete GPU capabilities. Benchmark data indicates solid single-core metrics, achieving a 1489.0 Geekbench single-core score and 28.04 GB/sec gzip compression. Multi-threaded and memory throughput metrics fall into the lower bands due to the dual-thread core limitation, with Geekbench multi-core scoring 1757.0 and Redis reaching 1.97 million SET operations per second. The server offers cost-effective access to direct-attached NVMe storage, making it well-suited for lightweight web services, caching tiers, temporary data processing, and microservice hosts requiring fast local scratch disks.
